title: The patient asks for a discount: receptionist requests, doctor approves
aim: The rule is that the receptionist cannot give a discount; only the doctor can. Test the hand-off: set up a draft bill, let the receptionist request a ₹300 discount, see what she can still do, find out how the doctor learns about the request, approve it, and issue the bill.
pre: Fresh local database. The doctor finalises Tara's visit with one procedure (Scaling ₹1,500) and creates a draft bill. Setup uses the C1 repair in the test harness.
verdict: WORKS, but the doctor is never told and the total changes before approval
summary: The two-step rule is enforced: the receptionist can only request; the doctor sees an 'Approve discount' button; after approval the bill is issued with the discount (₹1,500 - ₹300 = ₹1,200). Weak points: the draft total already drops to ₹1,200 while the request is still 'waiting for doctor approval'; nothing on the doctor's Today or anywhere else says a request is waiting; and the screen is unstyled with internal text.

problems.text: The doctor is not told. After the receptionist's request the doctor's Today page has no mention of a discount (checked: no 'discount' text anywhere). The doctor only finds the request by opening that specific bill.
problems.why: The patient waits at the desk while the receptionist walks to the doctor to say 'please open the bill'. The point of the approval step is lost.
problems.fix: Put 'Discount waiting: Tara Testcase ₹300' on the doctor's Today (and a count in the nav), with an Approve button.

problems.text: As soon as the receptionist presses Request discount, the draft bill shows 'Discount -₹300' and 'Total ₹1,200', while the line below still says 'waiting for doctor approval'.
problems.why: The receptionist may quote or even collect the lower total before the doctor said yes. The total should stay ₹1,500 until approval.
problems.fix: Show the requested discount in a separate line 'Requested (not approved): ₹300' and keep the total at ₹1,500.

problems.text: With the request waiting, the receptionist's 'Issue bill' button is still on screen; an attempt to click it in an earlier run timed out, so it is probably disabled, but nothing says why.
problems.why: A grey button without a reason.
problems.fix: Under the button: 'Waiting for the doctor to approve the discount.'

problems.text: The draft bill screen is the unstyled one (bullets, bare inputs, bare select) and carries two internal sentences: 'This is not a GST invoice (gst_mode off — DRAFT accountant).' and 'Discounts are not advertised. Billing decision only (DCI).'
problems.why: Staff-facing screen with legal and developer notes the receptionist cannot act on.
problems.fix: Build to mockup S09; move the notes to Settings > Billing.

problems.text: After 'Approve discount' there is no toast; the only change is the small line '₹300 · Hardship · approved'.
problems.why: The doctor cannot tell at a glance that it worked.

problems.text: Discount reason is a drop-down of four fixed reasons (Hardship, Staff or family, Courtesy, Other) with no space to write why when 'Other' is chosen.
problems.why: The audit trail has no explanation for 'Other'.
problems.fix: Show a text box when 'Other' is chosen.

good: The rule holds: the receptionist can request, only the doctor can approve (Approve discount appears only for the doctor).
The discount ends up on the issued bill: Subtotal ₹1,500, Discount -₹300, Total ₹1,200, number SB-2627-000025.
Reason is required and shown with the request ('₹300 · Hardship · waiting for doctor approval').
notTested: Rejecting a discount, a discount bigger than the bill, a discount on an issued bill.
Whether the receptionist can still edit items after requesting a discount.
The audit log entry for the approval.
